title: Fix missing res[:]=0 reset in stencil_poisson_harmonic
description: stencil_poisson resets a pre-allocated res buffer with res[:]=0 before accumulating, but stencil_poisson_harmonic does not. In _compiled_step, tmp_core is reused every iteration as the pre-allocated res, so from iteration 2 onward the accumulation starts from a stale value giving wrong results. Add res[:]=0 in the else branch when res is not None.

title: Phase 1 — Parameter audit
description: Read gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py and gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py to confirm: (1) the z-index and potential of the grid plane (pp_loweredge + pcb_width), (2) that barr[:,:,-1]=1 is the only cathode BC, (3) exact parameter names for phi_grid, phi_cathode, and domain spacing. Produce a table of confirmed values used as input to all subsequent phases. Decide whether BulkField (50 V/mm) should be a hardcoded constant or a new JSON config key (recommend JSON).
notes:
## Parameter Audit Results

### Grid plane z-index
Both generators place the grid (PCB shield) at:
  z_grid = pp_loweredge + pcb_width
With nGridPoints=10 (spacing=0.1 mm), pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition=2 mm, PcbWidth=1.6 mm:
  pp_loweredge = 2/0.1 = 20 (index)
  pcb_width = 1.6/0.1 = 16 (index)
  z_grid = 36 (index)

### Confirmed parameter table

| Parameter JSON key        | Value (JSON)   | Index units (nGridPoints=10) | Notes                              |
|--------------------------|----------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition | 2 mm          | 20                           | lower edge of pixel plane          |
| PcbWidth                  | 1.6 mm        | 16                           | PCB/grid thickness                 |
| z_grid (derived)          | —             | 36 (= 20+16)                 | grid plane z-index                 |
| GridPotential             | -1000 V       | —                            | potential on grid/PCB shield plane |
| CathodePotential          | -1300 V       | —                            | drift gen only                     |
| pixelSize                 | 3.5 mm        | 35                           |                                    |
| pixelGap                  | 0.9 mm        | 9                            |                                    |
| pixelPlaneWidth           | 0.1 mm        | 1                            |                                    |
| Npixels                   | 9             | —                            |                                    |
| LArPermittivity           | 1.505         | —                            | dimensionless eps_r                |
| FR4Permittivity           | 4.4           | —                            | dimensionless eps_r                |
| driftZDepth               | 28.0 mm       | 280                          |                                    |
| nGridPoints               | 10 pts/mm     | —                            | spacing = 0.1 mm                  |

### Cathode BC
- gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py: barr[:,:,-1]=1 (last z-plane = cathode) ✓
- gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py: barr[:,:,0]=1 (z=0 = cathode) — opposite z-convention!

### BulkField recommendation
BulkField=50 V/mm is NOT currently a JSON key. It is implicit: (CathodePotential - GridPotential)/driftZDepth = 300V/28mm ≈ 10.7 V/mm (not 50 V/mm — may need different config for 50 V/mm target). Recommend adding BulkField as a JSON config key for near-far domain separation, so it can be set independently of the absolute potentials.
close_reason: Audit complete: parameter table confirmed, cathode BC verified, BulkField recommendation recorded in notes

title: Fix spurious FR4/LAr epsilon interface in pixel aperture for harmonic stencil
description:
## Problem
In gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py generator(), line 427 sets ALL cells below z=pp_loweredge (z<2mm) to FR4 permittivity (eps=4.5), including cells inside the pixel aperture (the rounded-square hole through the PCB). Physically those aperture cells are filled with LAr (eps=1.5), not solid PCB.

The harmonic stencil (stencil_poisson_harmonic) uses the eps array for weighted averages at cell interfaces. The spurious FR4/LAr step at iz=19/20 inside the aperture creates:
1. A wrong dielectric discontinuity inside the aperture that modifies the potential above z=2mm, generating a lateral E-field component that deflects near-center paths outward.
2. A weaker bounce-back force below the pixel plane (eps-reduced E_z in FR4), so overshoot paths go deeper (z=1.73mm vs z=1.87mm), accumulating more lateral drift before recovering.

Net result: paths starting 0.22mm past the pixel center (first grid point past center in both x and y) converge on an attractor at the quarter-pixel center (~3.12mm local = pixel_center + pixel_size/4), producing the long unphysical horizontal excursions visible in the harmonic drift-path plots.

The circular and square gridHoleShape cases already fix this (lines 434-437 correcting aperture cells back to LAr), but GridHoleShape='None' has no such correction.

## Fix
After draw_pixel_plane() at line 446, add:
  if epsilon is not None:
      aperture_xy = (barr[:, :, pp_loweredge] == 0)  # free = inside pixel aperture
      epsilon[aperture_xy, :pp_loweredge] = LArPermittivity

This mirrors what the circular hole case does (line 437) for the 'None' gridHoleShape case.
close_reason: Fixed: added aperture_xy correction after draw_pixel_plane() to reset aperture cells to LArPermittivity

title: Determine correct permittivity units for FDM solver in WireCell unit system
description:
Before fixing the epsilon array generation (pochoir-qa1), verify what quantity and units the FDM solver expects for the permittivity array, and confirm the JSON config values are correct.

Investigation steps:
1. Confirm pochoir uses the WireCell unit system (units.py has mm=1, MeV=1, eplus=1). Derive epsilon_0 in WireCell units: epsilon_0_SI = 8.854e-12 F/m; compute epsilon_0 = 8.854e-12 * farad/meter numerically using units.py values.

2. Determine whether stencil_poisson_harmonic expects:
   (a) Relative permittivity epsilon_r (dimensionless, e.g. 1.5 for LAr, 4.5 for FR4), OR
   (b) Absolute permittivity epsilon = epsilon_r * epsilon_0 in WireCell units.
   Key insight: in the update rule phi[i] = sum(eps[i+-1/2]*phi[i+-1]) / sum(eps[i+-1/2]), epsilon_0 cancels from numerator and denominator — so only relative values matter for a pure Laplace solve. Absolute epsilon would only matter if a charge-density source term rho is added.

3. Confirm physical values in JSON are reasonable:
   - LArPermittivity = 1.5 (LAr epsilon_r ~ 1.505 at 87K)
   - FR4Permittivity = 4.5 (FR4 epsilon_r ~ 3.8-4.8)

4. Record conclusion with 'bd remember' and update pochoir-qa1 with the confirmed unit convention before implementing.
close_reason: Confirmed: solver uses relative permittivity (eps_r), eps_0 cancels in update rule. JSON values are correct.

title: Validate stencil_poisson_harmonic with epsilon=1 matches standard stencil

Validation procedure:
1. Run the small domain (POCHOIR_DRIFT_SHAPE=22,22,200) twice:
   a. Without --epsilon (standard stencil_poisson)
   b. With --epsilon pointing to an array of ones
2. Compare the two resulting potentials — they should agree to numerical precision.

To create the epsilon=1 array: either add a CLI option or a small helper script that generates a store entry filled with numpy.ones(domain.shape) at a given path (e.g. initial/drift3d_epsilon_ones), then pass that path via --epsilon.

This phase sits between Phase 4 (epsilon plumbing working) and Phase 6 (smoke test with real permittivity), and provides a fast sanity check that the harmonic code path is correct before introducing the LAr/FR4 contrast.
close_reason: Added test/test_stencil_poisson_harmonic.py; all 5 tests pass, confirming harmonic stencil with uniform eps=1 matches standard stencil_poisson to 1e-12.

title: Fix epsilon array generation for GridHoleShape=None
description:
In gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py, epsilon is only created when GridHoleShape is 'circular' or 'square'. With the current JSON config (GridHoleShape=None), no epsilon is stored so initial/drift3d_epsilon never exists.

Geometry convention:
- z=0: anode-side face of the domain
- z=1500 (z_max): cathode plane
- Pixel plane occupies z = [pp_loweredge : pp_loweredge+pp_width]
- PCB (FR4) slab is BELOW the pixel plane, i.e. at z = [0 : pp_loweredge]
- LAr drift region is ABOVE the pixel plane, i.e. at z = [pp_loweredge+pp_width : z_max]

Fix: always create epsilon when LArPermittivity and FR4Permittivity are present in config:
1. Fill entire array with LArPermittivity (safe default)
2. Set z = [0 : pp_loweredge] to FR4Permittivity (PCB slab below pixel plane)
3. For 'circular' or 'square' GridHoleShape, carve holes in the PCB back to LArPermittivity as before

The existing partial code (epsilon[:, :, pp_loweredge+pp_width+pcb_width+1:] = LArPermittivity) had the PCB location wrong and left large regions as zero — replace entirely with the above.
notes: Confirmed: use dimensionless relative permittivity. LArPermittivity=1.5, FR4Permittivity=4.5 are correct as-is. No unit conversion needed.
close_reason: Fixed: always create epsilon when LArPermittivity/FR4Permittivity present; fill with LArPermittivity, set z=[0:pp_loweredge] to FR4Permittivity; fixed hole carving range for circular case.

title: G3: Fix circular hole epsilon in gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py (FR4 slab + tiling)
description:
Files: pochoir/gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py only.

In gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py the epsilon array for circular holes is partially constructed but broken:
- Line 427: FR4 slab assignment is commented out.
- Lines 433-438: quarter-circle hole mask is applied for corner positions (cx,cy) at the full-array corners (0,0), (Nx-1,0), etc. This is wrong — for a tiled grid of n_pix pixels, there are n_pix² holes to carve, not 4 corner quarter-holes. This was copied from draw_pcb_plane which draws a single-pixel-cell grid; the drift generator covers the full n_pix × n_pix footprint.

Changes required:
(a) Uncomment and correct the FR4 slab: epsilon[:, :, pp_loweredge+pp_width : pp_loweredge+pp_width+pcb_width] = FR4Permittivity. Verify z-range.
(b) Replace the corner-only hole mask with a full n_pix × n_pix tiled carving:
    - For each pixel cell (i, j) in the grid, compute the hole center in index space.
    - Build the circular hole mask using the same r1 radius and mgrid distance test as draw_pcb_plane.
    - Set epsilon[mask, pp_loweredge+pp_width : pp_loweredge+pp_width+pcb_width] = LArPermittivity.
(c) Set LAr above shield (already on line 428 — confirm it is correct).

Acceptance: at z_mid in the PCB slab, every circular hole voxel is LArPermittivity and the surrounding FR4 ring is FR4Permittivity.

title: G1: Audit and fix circular hole epsilon in gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py
description:
Files: pochoir/gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py only.

The circular hole epsilon path (lines 236-288) exists but needs a careful audit before it is relied upon:

(a) Verify z-range correctness: z_pcb_start = pp_loweredge + pp_width, z_pcb_end = pp_loweredge + pp_width + pcb_width. Confirm these are inclusive/exclusive correctly and that z_lar_above = z_pcb_end + 1 is consistent with what barr sets as the shield-grid electrode z-plane (pp_loweredge + pcb_width).
(b) Verify hole carving: the fill_area calls (barr1..barr4) carve holes in one pixel tile. Confirm the tile shape matches (dom.shape[0] // n_pix, dom.shape[1] // n_pix) and that the hole boundary (form_quarter_boundary) represents the interior of the hole, not its perimeter.
(c) Verify tiling: the loop (lines 272-276) copies epsilon[:shape[0], :shape[1], z_pcb_start:z_pcb_end] across the grid. Confirm there are no off-by-one issues when n_pix does not divide dom.shape evenly.
(d) Confirm epsilon below z_pcb_start (pixel plane and below) is left as 0 — this is the region below the shield, which is not physically meaningful but must not accidentally interfere with the solver.
(e) Fix any issues found. Add a brief inline comment at each z-range assignment explaining which physical layer it corresponds to.
close_reason: Fixed draw_3Dstrips z-arg (pp_loweredge+pcb_width→pp_loweredge+pp_width), removed debug plot, added z-range comments. 6 unit tests pass.

title: S5: Pass epsilon to all solver engines in __main__.py
description:
Files: pochoir/__main__.py only.

Currently __main__.py passes epsilon only to the torch solver (line ~405). The numpy, cupy, and cumba solve() calls (added in S2/S3/S4) also accept epsilon but are not given it here.

Changes required:
(a) Locate every non-torch call to a solver's solve() inside the 'solve' CLI command and add epsilon=eps as a keyword argument. The variable eps is already retrieved from the store at line ~353.
(b) Verify the epsilon store retrieval at line ~353: it must return a numpy array (not a metadata wrapper). Check the ctx.obj.get() call and unwrap correctly.
(c) The torch path (line ~405) already passes epsilon=eps — confirm it is unchanged.
(d) If the selected engine does not support epsilon yet and eps is not None, emit a logging warning rather than silently ignoring it.

Acceptance: running 'pochoir solve --engine numpy --epsilon my_eps ...' does not raise TypeError and passes the array into fdm_numpy.solve().

title: S4: Add harmonic CUDA kernel and epsilon support to fdm_cumba.solve()
description:
Files: pochoir/fdm_cumba.py only.

fdm_cumba uses a custom @cuda.jit kernel (stencil_numba3d_jit) that cannot call the generic numpy/cupy stencil_poisson_harmonic directly. A new CUDA jit kernel must be written.

Changes required:
(a) Write a new @cuda.jit kernel 'stencil_harmonic_numba3d_jit(arr, eps, out)' that:
    - Computes the harmonic-mean interface permittivities for the 6 face-neighbours:
      e_pos = 2*eps[i,j,k]*eps[i+1,j,k] / (eps[i,j,k] + eps[i+1,j,k])  (and similarly for -x, ±y, ±z)
    - Sets out[i,j,k] = (sum of e_face * phi_neighbour) / (sum of e_face) for interior cells.
(b) Add a 'stencil_harmonic' dispatch function analogous to the existing 'stencil' function, which launches stencil_harmonic_numba3d_jit with the same block/grid config.
(c) Add 'epsilon=None' to solve(), pad epsilon with cupy when provided, and branch inside the solve loop to call stencil_harmonic vs stencil.

Acceptance: uniform epsilon gives same result as vanilla stencil. Division-by-zero guard is not needed when epsilon > 0 everywhere, but confirm this holds for the LAr/FR4 value range.
close_reason: Implemented stencil_harmonic_numba3d_jit kernel and epsilon=None branch in solve(); fixed pre-existing cuda.grid(2)->grid(3) and 16^3->8^3 thread block bugs; early-return path now calls .get(). Tests pass.

title: S3: Add epsilon support to fdm_cupy.solve()
description:
Files: pochoir/fdm_cupy.py only.

fdm_cupy.solve() uses the same vanilla stencil call pattern as fdm_numpy. stencil_poisson_harmonic in fdm_generic.py uses arrays.module(phi) which already dispatches correctly for cupy arrays — no new kernel is needed.

Changes required:
(a) Add 'epsilon=None' as an explicit keyword argument to solve().
(b) When epsilon is not None, convert it to cupy and pad: epsilon_pad = cupy.pad(cupy.array(epsilon), 1).
(c) Import stencil_poisson_harmonic from .fdm_generic at the top of the file.
(d) Inside the solve loop, branch on epsilon_pad: call stencil(iarr_pad, tmp_core) when None, call stencil_poisson_harmonic(iarr_pad, epsilon_pad, res=tmp_core) otherwise.
(e) Return values converted with .get() as before.

Acceptance: same uniform-epsilon test as S2, on GPU.

title: S2: Add epsilon support to fdm_numpy.solve()
description:
Files: pochoir/fdm_numpy.py only.

fdm_numpy.solve() currently ignores epsilon entirely — its **kwargs swallow it silently. The stencil call is always the vanilla stencil(iarr) regardless of whether epsilon is provided.

Changes required:
(a) Add 'epsilon=None' as an explicit keyword argument to solve().
(b) When epsilon is not None, pad it the same way iarr is padded (numpy.pad(epsilon, 1)).
(c) Import stencil_poisson_harmonic from .fdm_generic alongside the existing stencil import.
(d) Inside the solve loop, replace the unconditional stencil(iarr) call with a branch: if epsilon_pad is None call stencil(iarr, res=tmp), else call stencil_poisson_harmonic(iarr, epsilon_pad, res=tmp).
(e) The rest of the loop (boundary restore, edge_condition, neumann_condition) is unchanged.

Acceptance: calling solve() with a uniform epsilon array of all-ones gives the same result as calling it without epsilon (within floating-point tolerance).

title: Phase 3b: Verify shield grid electrode geometry (barr) is consistent with hole masks across both generators
description:
After Phases 3 and 4 implement the hole masks, this phase verifies that the shield grid electrode boundary conditions (barr) are physically consistent with the material geometry (epsilon) in both generators.

The shield grid electrode occupies the FR4 material surrounding each hole — NOT the interior of the through-holes. If barr marks hole voxels as electrodes, or if the FR4 slab z-range used for epsilon differs from the z-range used for barr, the physics will be wrong regardless of how correctly epsilon is set.

Checks:
(a) For every voxel where barr==1 (shield grid electrode), verify epsilon==FR4Permittivity (electrode sits in FR4, not LAr).
(b) For every voxel inside a through-hole at the shield grid z-range, verify barr==0 (holes are free interior points) and epsilon==LArPermittivity.
(c) Cross-check: the total solid-angle fraction of holes should match the HoleRadius / pixel pitch geometry analytically.
(d) Produce a 2D cross-section plot showing barr and epsilon side by side at the mid-plane of the PCB layer for visual inspection.
(e) Tests must pass for both circular and square hole shapes, for both gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid and gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.

Additionally: (a) verify the --epsilon CLI flag and store retrieval (line 353) work for all code paths, (b) ensure the epsilon array is stored by gen_pcb_* generators with the correct taxon key so the solve step can retrieve it, (c) add a warning if epsilon is provided but the chosen engine does not support it (before Phase 2 fully closes). (d) Verify that the shield grid electrode boundaries (barr) are physically consistent with the hole geometry for both shapes — the electrode should be on the FR4 ring around each hole, not inside the through-hole.

title: Phase 3: Implement complete shield grid FR4 + hole geometry in gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py
description:
The shield grid is a PCB layer (FR4 material) sitting above the pixel collection plane, with through-holes aligned to pixels that allow field lines to pass. In gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py the FR4 permittivity assignment is commented out (line ~427) because it was only valid in the absence of holes. This phase must implement the full geometry:

(a) Uncomment and correctly set the FR4 base slab epsilon for the PCB z-range (pp_loweredge+pp_width to pp_loweredge+pp_width+pcb_width).
(b) Build a Boolean hole mask from the existing hole-drawing geometry (fill_area / HoleRadius / GridHoleShape) for both circular and square hole shapes.
(c) Carve holes through the FR4 slab in epsilon: set epsilon=LArPermittivity inside holes.
(d) Tile the single-pixel epsilon pattern across the full Npixels grid.
(e) Verify barr (boundary condition mask for the shield grid electrode) is consistent with the hole geometry — the shield grid electrode lives on the FR4 boundary rings around each hole, not inside the holes.

This phase is a prerequisite for correct permittivity arrays AND for verifying that the shield grid boundary conditions (barr) are physically consistent with the material geometry.

title: Phase 2: Wire permittivity (epsilon) through all FDM solver backends
description: Currently only fdm_torch.py has a branch to call stencil_poisson_harmonic when epsilon is provided. fdm_numpy.py, fdm_cupy.py, and fdm_cumba.py all ignore epsilon entirely. Each backend's solve loop must be updated so that when an epsilon array is passed: (a) it is padded/sliced consistently with iarr, (b) stencil_poisson_harmonic is called in place of stencil_poisson, (c) the epsilon array is handled correctly for device (GPU vs CPU) in cupy/cumba. Acceptance: running the solver with a homogeneous epsilon=1 array gives bit-identical results to running without epsilon.

title: Assign high permittivity (eps_r=1e10) to pixel pad voxels to approximate conductor shielding
description:
## Why this issue exists

The pixel pads in the detector geometry act as conductor-like shields. The current FDM setup assigns fixed-potential boundary conditions to pixel pad voxels but leaves their epsilon at LArPermittivity (1.5). To approximate conductor behavior (which drives E→0 inside the metal) without a full conductor BC formulation, assign a very large relative permittivity (eps_r = 1e10) to the pixel pad voxels. This makes the harmonic-averaged interface weights at pixel boundaries dominate, reducing the effective field in the region z < pixel plane.

## What needs to be done

1. Add a new config key `PixelPermittivity` (default 1e10) to the JSON config schema.
2. In `gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py` (lines 420-452): after the FR4 slab and aperture-correction steps, identify the pixel pad voxels and assign `epsilon[pad_mask] = PixelPermittivity`.
3. In `gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py` (lines 235-248): apply the same assignment for the non-drift variant.
4. The pixel pad mask is the set of voxels where `barr[:,:, pp_loweredge : pp_loweredge+pp_width] != 0` — i.e., boundary cells in the pixel plane z-slab.
5. Update example JSON configs to include the new key.
6. Verify with a test run that the epsilon array has 1e10 in the correct voxels and that the FDM solve completes without divergence.

## Acceptance criteria

- `PixelPermittivity` key accepted by both generators; defaults to 1e10 if absent.
- Pixel pad voxels in the epsilon array are set to 1e10 after `gen`.
- FR4 and LAr regions are unaffected.
- Aperture (hole) voxels remain at LArPermittivity (not overwritten by pixel assignment).
- FDM solve converges without NaN/Inf.
- Test run with example config passes.
design:
## Design decisions

### Pixel pad mask
Use `barr[:,:, pp_loweredge : pp_loweredge+pp_width] != 0` to identify pixel pad voxels. This is already computed during geometry generation — no new geometry logic needed. The aperture correction in the current code (line 452) sets LAr eps for apertures, so ordering matters: apply PixelPermittivity AFTER the aperture correction so apertures stay at LArPermittivity.

### Config default — BACKWARD COMPAT
Default to LArPermittivity (not 1e10): `cfg.get('PixelPermittivity', cfg.get('LArPermittivity', 1.5))`. Existing configs without the key reproduce the original behavior exactly, allowing direct before/after comparison by only adding the key to configs where the new physics is desired.

### Both generators
`gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py` and `gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py` both produce epsilon arrays and must both be updated. The drift variant (lines 420-452) is the primary target; the static variant (lines 235-248) follows the same pattern.

### No stencil changes
The existing `stencil_poisson_harmonic` handles large eps values correctly — harmonic averaging at interfaces with eps_j→∞ gives 2*eps_i, which is finite and well-conditioned. No changes to the solver.

### Numerical concern: NaN risk
eps=1e10 in harmonic averaging: eps_half = 2*eps_i*eps_j/(eps_i+eps_j). For eps_j=1e10, eps_i=1.5: eps_half ≈ 3.0. No overflow in float32. Safe.

### Ordering of epsilon assignments (drift variant)
1. Initialize entire domain to LArPermittivity (existing line 425)
2. Set FR4 slab (existing line 427)
3. Restore LAr in circular holes in FR4 (existing lines 430-437)
4. Restore LAr in apertures (existing line 452)
5. **NEW**: Set pixel pad voxels to PixelPermittivity (default = LArPermittivity → no-op when key absent)
notes:
## Key file locations

- `pochoir/gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py` lines 420-452: epsilon construction (primary)
- `pochoir/gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py` lines 235-248: epsilon construction (secondary)
- `pochoir/fdm_generic.py` lines 134-194: stencil_poisson_harmonic (no changes needed)
- `test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_eps.json`: example config to update
- `test/example_gen_pixel_with_grid.json`: example config to update

## Pixel plane geometry recap
- Z-range: `[pp_loweredge, pp_loweredge + pp_width]`
- pp_loweredge = int(pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition / spacing)
- pp_width = int(pixelPlaneWidth / spacing)
- Pixel pads: barr != 0 in that z-slab
- Apertures (inter-pixel gaps): barr == 0 in that z-slab → remain at LArPermittivity
close_reason: Implemented and verified. PixelPermittivity key added to both generators with default=LArPermittivity. Smoke test confirms pad voxels get correct eps, no-op when key absent.

title: 2-stage coarse-to-fine FDM test: (44,44,300) drift + (396,396,300) weight
description:
Design and implement a 2-stage coarse-to-fine FDM test using 1mm (coarse) → 0.1mm (fine) spacing for both drift and weighting field domains.

## Domains
- Drift: (44,44,300) at 0.1mm = 4.4×4.4×30mm physical
- Weight: (396,396,300) at 0.1mm = 39.6×39.6×30mm physical

## Coarse stage shapes (computed by _stage_shape)
- Drift coarse (1mm): (5,5,31)
- Weight coarse (1mm): (41,41,31)

## Config files to create
Base from: test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json and test/example_gen_pixel_with_grid.json

### Drift config changes (2 changes only):
- CathodePotential: -7500 → -1400  (50 V/mm × 28mm drift depth)
- driftZDepth: 148.0 → 28.0  (cathode at z=30mm minus pixel plane at z=2mm)

### Weight config changes (1 change only):
- driftZDepth: 148.0 → 28.0

All other parameters verified correct:
- pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition: 2mm (already correct, pixel plane at z=2mm)
- pixelSize: 3.5mm + pixelGap: 0.9mm = 4.4mm = domain X pitch ✓
- GridHoleShape: None → PcbWidth, HoleRadius, LArPermittivity, FR4Permittivity all inactive
- pixelPlaneWidth 0.1mm → 0 grid units at coarse (pp_width=0), but z2=pp_loweredge+1 so still 1 layer thick ✓
- chamfer_r 0.7mm → 0 grid units at coarse, trimCorner loop range(0) does nothing ✓
- Npixels=9: only used for dims computation which is unused in boundary-setting code

## Test script to create
test/test-2stage-ctf.sh with:
- pochoir fdm-multires --target-shape 44,44,300 --target-spacing 0.1 --stages 2 --coarsest-spacing 1.0 --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid --engine numpy --precision 2e-8 --epoch 1000000 --edges per,per,fix
- pochoir fdm-multires --target-shape 396,396,300 --target-spacing 0.1 --stages 2 --coarsest-spacing 1.0 --generator pcb_pixel_with_grid --engine numpy --precision 2e-8 --epoch 5000000 --edges per,per,fix
- downstream: pochoir velo, pochoir paths, pochoir induce

## Verification
1. potential_L0 (1mm stage) exists and looks smooth
2. potential_L1 (0.1mm stage) matches boundary conditions
3. Downstream velo/paths/induce complete successfully
close_reason: Stopped: fdm-multires generates at fine resolution (396,396,300) causing unacceptable memory/time cost. Branch approach deemed too weak. Will restart from a clean branch in a new session.

title: Phase 5: Integrate neumann_condition into all FDM solvers
description: Update all four solver backends to call neumann_condition after each stencil update, in the same place edge_condition is called. Files: fdm_numpy.py, fdm_torch.py, fdm_cupy.py, fdm_cumba.py. The solve() function signature must accept an optional narr/normal_axis/normal_dir argument (or a single NeumannSpec object). When narr is None, behavior is unchanged (backward compatible). The padded-array variants (torch, cupy, cumba) must also handle the padding offset correctly when indexing narr.

title: Phase 6: Update __main__.py and solver entry points to pass narr through
description: pochoir/__main__.py and any CLI entry points that load arr/barr from JSON configs and call the solver need to also load narr (if present) and pass it to solve(). Update config loading, the solve() call, and any intermediate wrappers. If narr is absent from config (legacy runs), default to None so old workflows are unaffected.

title: Phase 3: Add Neumann gap mask output to gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py
description: Modify pochoir/gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py to generate and return a narr (Neumann array) alongside arr and barr. narr should be 1 at all (x,y) positions in the pixel plane z-layer where barr=0 (gap cells), and 0 elsewhere. The normal axis is z (axis=2 in standard layout) and normal direction points away from the pixel plane into the LAr region. Update the generator's return value and any downstream config/JSON output so callers receive narr.

title: Phase 4: Add Neumann gap mask output to gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py
description: Same as Phase 3 but for pochoir/gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py (the drift field version). Identify the pixel plane z-layer, mark gap cells (barr=0 in that layer) in narr, set normal axis/direction to z pointing into LAr. Return narr alongside arr, barr, epsilon. Keep consistent with the interface change made in Phase 3.

title: Phase 2: Design neumann_condition function in fdm_generic.py
description: Design and implement a neumann_condition(arr, neumann_mask, normal_axis, normal_dir) function in pochoir/fdm_generic.py. The function should: for each cell flagged in neumann_mask, copy the potential value from the neighboring cell one step inward along normal_axis (direction normal_dir = +1 or -1). This enforces dphi/dn = 0 at those cells each solver iteration. The signature should be compatible with how edge_condition is called across fdm_numpy.py, fdm_torch.py, fdm_cupy.py, fdm_cumba.py. Consider whether the mask should store the axis/direction or whether those are passed separately. Must handle torch/cupy/numpy array types.

title: Phase 1: Audit gap geometry and boundary representation in gen_pcb files
description: Carefully read gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py and gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py to map exactly which z-layer(s) the pixel plane occupies, how barr marks pixel pads, and what cells constitute the inter-pixel gaps. Document: the z-index of the pixel plane, the (x,y) extent of gap cells vs pad cells, and which array index direction corresponds to the normal of the pixel plane. This audit is prerequisite for all other phases.

title: Phase 4: Update example JSON config files with the new start-point keys
description: Add driftZDepth, nGridPoints, and gridSpacing (optional) to the example/template JSON config files in the repo so users know what keys are available. Update any shell scripts (e.g. test-full-3d-pixel.sh) that call the starts command with --mode yes to also pass --config pointing at the relevant JSON.
close_reason: Added driftZDepth/nGridPoints to 8 pixel JSON configs (test/ and test/configs_json/); updated test-full-3d-pixel.sh starts call to pass -c example_gen_pixel_with_grid.json
